claim: ruff S603 (subprocess untrusted input) at updater.py:595,598,600,967
rationale: All flagged subprocess.run() calls use list-form argv (never shell=True), with hardcoded command names (dbus-send, systemctl, bash) and locally-generated paths (tempfile, ENGINE resolved next to updater.py). No user-controlled input flows into any argv, so shell/command injection is not reachable. S603 fires on every subprocess call regardless of actual risk; safe for this desktop GUI.

claim: ruff S607 (partial executable path) at updater.py:629,652,653,656,663,967
rationale: Flags use of bare tool names (systemctl, dbus-send, bash) resolved via PATH. These are standard trusted system binaries for a Linux desktop app; using absolute paths would be non-portable across distros. No attacker-controlled PATH is in scope (single-user desktop session). Intended behaviour, not a lookalike-binary risk.

claim: shellcheck SC2001 at update_system.sh:267 (use ${//} instead of sed)
rationale: The sed is `echo "$dupe" | sed 's/^/      /'` which prefixes every line of a multi-line variable using the per-line ^ anchor. Bash ${var//search/replace} cannot match a line-start anchor across multiple lines, so sed is the correct tool here, not a stylistic slip. No change warranted.

claim: pyright/mypy (~32) "type[Qt] has no attribute AlignVCenter / QProcess.MergedChannels / bytes(QByteArray)"
rationale: These are PySide6 type-stub scoping gaps, not runtime bugs. Short-form enum access (Qt.AlignVCenter, Qt.PointingHandCursor, QProcess.MergedChannels) and bytes(QByteArray) are all valid and work at runtime in PySide6/Qt6; the bundled .pyi stubs just don't expose them at that scope. No pyproject/type-check config exists in the project, so these are not gating CI. Suppress unless the project adopts fully-scoped enum idioms project-wide.

claim: tests/run-tests.sh:1360 — isolation defect via a shell-out (pre-pass pattern `system_shell_out`)
rationale: Line 1360 is a plain banner: echo "TEST: a non-English locale still detects an up-to-date system (LC_ALL pinned)". The pattern is looking for C's system() call and matched the literal substring "system (" inside English prose. No shell-out, no engine call, no export at or near that line; the scenario below it goes through run_engine normally. Pattern is language-inappropriate for a .sh file, where system() cannot occur.

claim: tests/bump-test.py:95 and tests/docs-check.py:230 — error_handling defect at the final exit (pre-pass pattern `cpp_exit`)
rationale: Both lines are `sys.exit(main())`, the correct Python idiom for propagating a status code. bump-test.py:91 returns `1 if failed else 0`; docs-check.py:226 returns `1 if failures else 0`. Nothing is swallowed — the exit code faithfully reflects the tally. The pattern is aimed at C/C++ `exit()` calls buried mid-test and does not apply to a module's `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard.

claim: tests/gui-smoke.py:57 and :1361 — error_handling defect at exit (pre-pass pattern `cpp_exit`)
rationale: Line 57 is `sys.exit(77)` on ImportError — the documented skip-for-absent-tool convention (77 is read as "skipped" by local-CI.sh:38-44 and .github/workflows/release.yml:33, all three verified to agree). Line 1361 is `sys.exit(code)` where code is `1 if FAIL else 0`. Neither swallows a failure; both are the intended exit-code contract described in docs/standards/testing.md §1.

claim: tests/gui-smoke.py:89 — flakiness from a fixed sleep (pre-pass patterns `sleep_call` / `posix_sleep`)
rationale: The `time.sleep(0.02)` at :89 is the body of `_wait_for_notify`'s poll loop (`while time.monotonic() < deadline`), i.e. the poll-with-timeout pattern the standard prescribes — not a blind sleep guessing a duration. On timeout it returns False, so the caller's check() goes red rather than green. A separate, narrower residual risk (the 2.0s deadline racing a real subprocess spawn) is recorded as its own LOW finding rather than as this pattern hit.
